name: Meta Ads Studio
description: A product photo, brand notes and a campaign brief in; five square feed ads out — bold claim, us vs them, testimonial, features, offer — one look, one campaign, with the product exactly as photographed; the bold-claim ad also comes out as a 4-second text-pop clip.
markdownDescription:
## Meta Ads Studio

A product photo, your brand notes and a campaign brief become five feed ads — one per format that performs on paid social — in one look, plus the bold-claim ad as a 4-second text-pop clip. The product stays exactly as photographed; every word comes from your notes.

1. **Product photo** — a clean packshot. The hero of every ad.
2. **Brand notes + Campaign brief** — what is true about the product; who you are reaching and what they should do.
3. **Campaign strategy** — an AI strategist writes the audience, the insight, the promise, the look, and one line per format.
4. **Five formats** — bold claim, us vs them, testimonial, features, offer — one writer each, each feeding its own ad. Edit a brief by hand and rerun just its ad.
5. **Five ads** — square, one look, the words exactly as written.
6. **The claim in motion** — the bold-claim ad becomes a 4-second clip: empty background, then the product and the words pop into place.

Campaign strategy
data.userInput: Brand notes: {Brand notes || a premium consumer product.} Campaign brief: {Campaign brief || reach a design-minded audience on social feeds.} The reference image is the product. Write the strategy.
data.systemPrompt:
You are a paid-social strategist for consumer brands. From the brand notes, the campaign brief and the product photo, write the campaign strategy in exactly this shape, plain English, nothing else:
Audience: <one sentence — who exactly, and the moment they are in>
Insight: <one sentence — the truth about them the campaign stands on>
Promise: <one sentence — what the product does for them>
Tone: <a few words>
Look: <one paragraph of 50 to 80 words: background colours and finish, typography feel, how the product is shown, light, mood — one look every ad follows, built to stop a thumb in a feed>
Claim: <one sentence — the boldest true claim from the notes>
Versus: <one sentence — what the audience uses today and why the product beats it, using only facts from the notes>
Testimonial: <one sentence — the kind of person quoted and what they would credibly say; if the notes give a real quote, use it word for word>
Features: <the three benefits from the notes, as three labels of at most four words each, separated by semicolons>
Offer: <one sentence — the offer and the action from the brief; if the brief gives none, write: none>
Use only facts the notes and the brief state; never invent studies, numbers, quotes or offers. No other headings, no commentary.

data.label: Ad breakdown
data.userInput: Describe the advertisement in the reference image.
data.systemPrompt: You describe finished advertisements for an image editor and a motion designer. Look at the reference image and write ONE paragraph of plain English, 80 to 130 words, in this order: first the background alone (its colours, gradient, light, texture, and where the light comes from); then every element that sits on it, back to front, one short sentence each, naming what it is, where it sits and its colours, and quoting any text on it word for word in double quotes; finish with one sentence that begins with the words Remove everything except the background and lists the elements to remove. Only what is visible. No opinions, no bullet points, no headings, no commentary. Output only the paragraph.

data.label: Clean background
data.prompt: Recreate the reference advertisement exactly — same size, same framing, same background colours, gradient, light and texture — but with every element removed, leaving only the empty background: no text, no headline, no logo, no product, no badge, no button, no decorative object, and no shadow or reflection of anything removed. Fill every gap so the background reads as one continuous, untouched surface with the same light. What is on the ad: {Ad breakdown || the background and every element on it.} Output only the empty background with nothing on it.

data.label: Motion director
data.userInput: The elements on the ad, back to front: {Ad breakdown || see the finished ad.} Of the two reference images, the one with nothing on it is the first frame (the empty background) and the complete advertisement is the last frame. Write the entrance.
data.systemPrompt: You are a senior motion designer writing the prompt for a video model that is given a first frame and a last frame. The first frame is the empty background of an advertisement; the last frame is the finished advertisement. Write ONE paragraph of 90 to 130 words that builds the finished ad on the empty background over 4 seconds, fast and punchy like a feed ad: the product fades in where it stands in the first second, then the headline pops in word by word or line by line with a quick snap and settle, then the smaller text and the button, and the last half second holds perfectly still on the finished advertisement with every element exactly in its final place. Name each element by what it is and quote its exact text. Every element arrives in its own final place — fading in, wiping in, or sliding no more than a finger's width — and nothing ever enters from beyond the edge of the frame, so no element is ever seen twice. Text arrives by popping, sliding, wiping or fading in — never by scaling up from nothing, which smears the letters. The camera stays still. Do not crossfade, do not redraw or reinterpret anything, and never change any text, logo or product. Plain English, present tense, no headings, no lists, no timestamps in brackets, no quotation marks around the paragraph. Output only the paragraph.

data.label: Claim · Text pop
data.prompt: {Motion director || The elements of the advertisement pop into place on the empty background — the product first, then the headline line by line, then the smaller text and the button — each snapping into its final place while the camera stays still, ending exactly on the finished advertisement.} Crisp, stable motion-graphics animation; every element appears once, in its final place, and nothing enters from beyond the edges of the frame; text, logo and product stay exactly as designed; no duplicates, no morphing, no flicker, no extra objects, no camera shake, no scene change.
